item.title: Various untaxed cars, 11th August
item.description:
Dear sir/madam Subject: Formal Complaint – Suspected Car Sales Business and Damaged/Untaxed Vehicles at 41 Leechcroft Avenue, DA15 8RS Dear Sir/Madam, I am writing to raise a formal complaint regarding suspected car-dealing activity being operated from 41 Leechcroft Avenue, DA15 8RS. There are regularly a number of vehicles associated with this property being parked on the public road, including outside my home and outside the homes of neighbouring residents. The number of vehicles and the frequency with which they are parked and moved has become a concern for local residents. Some of these vehicles appear to have no current vehicle tax and/or no valid MOT. There are also vehicles that appear to be badly damaged or in poor condition, which are being left parked on the public highway. Some of the vehicles appear to have significant visible damage, and I am concerned about whether they are suitable and lawful to be kept or used on the road. There are also concerns regarding whether some of these vehicles are appropriately insured. I understand that insurance and vehicle taxation may fall under the responsibility of other authorities, but I would be grateful if this information could be passed to the relevant enforcement body where appropriate. I am concerned that a vehicle-sales business may be operating from this residential property, with vehicles being stored and displayed for sale on the public road. This appears to be having an ongoing impact on the surrounding residents and the use of the street. I therefore respectfully ask Bexley Council to investigate whether: A car-sales or vehicle-trading business is being operated from 41 Leechcroft Avenue. The activity has the necessary planning permission or is permitted under the property's current use. The number of vehicles being stored at or around the property is appropriate for a residential premises. The damaged vehicles and other vehicles being left on the public highway are creating a nuisance or obstruction. Any environmental, planning or other local authority regulations are being breached. I would also ask that, where matters fall outside the Council's responsibility, the information is referred to the appropriate authority, such as the DVLA, police or other relevant enforcement body. I can provide photographs, vehicle registration numbers, dates and details of individual vehicles if required. I am also willing to provide further information about the frequency with which the vehicles are being brought to and removed from the property. I would be grateful if you could confirm receipt of this complaint and advise me of the reference number and which department will be investigating the matter. I would also appreciate it if my personal details could be kept confidential from the person being reported, where possible. I don’t like being the nosy neighbour but this is becoming a real problem now Inline image
Nearest road to the pin placed on the map (automatically generated by OpenStreetMap): 28, Leechcroft Avenue, Blackfen, Sidcup, Greater London

item.title: Fly‑Tipping Report – 1 Bostall Manorway, Abbey Wood, SE2 9EE, 11th August
item.description:
I am writing to report an ongoing fly‑tipping issue at 1 Bostall Manorway, Abbey Wood, SE2 9EE. I live in the first house at the entrance of the estate, and for several days now a large amount of rubbish has been dumped on the grass area directly outside the property. The waste has not been cleared, and as a result, other people have started adding more rubbish to the pile. The situation is getting worse and is now causing inconvenience, annoyance, and an unpleasant environment for the residents who live here. I kindly request that Greenwich Council send a team to remove the rubbish as soon as possible. Additionally, for many years I have asked the council to install a “No Dumping / No Rubbish” sign at this location. A clear sign would help prevent repeated fly‑tipping and keep the area clean for residents. Thank you for your assistance. I look forward to this being resolved.

Nearest address to the pin placed on the map (from OS Places API): Bostall Manorway, Abbey Wood

item.description:

It carries no reflective banding or markings of any kind, and it sits low on a dark, unlit corner where the paving is a similar dark colour, which makes it very difficult to see after dark. Local residents have told me it has been in this damaged state for a long time. My vehicle struck it in darkness on 2 March 2026 and sustained significant damage to the nearside. Please replace the bollard or, at minimum, fit reflective markings.
